overview: The MPS Meeting of the Whole is a deliberative body of the School Committee tasked with detailed fiscal planning, policy development, and executive evaluation for the Medford Public Schools. Throughout the 2022-2023 to 2026-2027 terms, the committee has primarily focused on navigating the transition from federal pandemic relief funding to municipal allocations. Its work includes the annual evaluation of the Superintendent, the development of district-wide non-discrimination policies, and the oversight of school building projects. As of early 2026, the body is focused on resolving a multi-million dollar gap in the FY27 budget and advancing the design phase of the high school construction project.

threads.name: Annual Budget Planning
threads.summary: The committee conducts multi-meeting reviews of the annual operating budget, starting with the $71.8 million FY24 proposal that addressed the initial loss of federal ESSER funds. For FY25, the body managed a $7.5 million spending pressure created by contractual obligations and underfunded operational accounts. Recent sessions for FY26 and FY27 have focused on 'right-sizing' maintenance and technology infrastructure, with the latest projections showing a $5 million gap relative to city funding.

threads.name: Superintendent Evaluation
threads.summary: In early 2023, the committee established nine focus indicators from the state rubric and created a new standing subcommittee to manage the evaluation process. The body reviewed self-evaluations and member data, eventually approving a composite rating of 'Proficient' for the Superintendent's 2022-2023 performance. The committee has since institutionalized the formal evaluation as a recurring annual agenda item for the month of June.

threads.name: High School Operations and Facilities
threads.summary: Following a consultant's report on high school culture and safety, the committee began overseeing administrative restructuring and the creation of new leadership committees for student behavior and diversity. This oversight expanded to the physical plant, with the body authorizing Statements of Interest for the MSBA Accelerated Repair Program to address roof and heating issues at elementary schools. Currently, the committee is reviewing design options for a comprehensive high school construction project.

threads.name: Financial Oversight and Revenue Management
threads.summary: To stabilize the district's long-term finances, the committee initiated a revenue collection audit and proposed a new methodology for charging administrative overhead to self-sustaining programs. Members regularly review revolving accounts for athletics, rentals, and the public pool to address persistent operating deficits. In 2026, the body authorized the payment of significant overdue electrical invoices that had been delayed due to past staffing transitions.

threads.name: Non-Discrimination Policy Development
threads.summary: The committee conducted a comprehensive review of Policy ACA-1 regarding gender identity to align district practices with state regulations. Key amendments included the standardization of 'caregiver' terminology and the clarification of student rights regarding record changes upon reaching age 14 or ninth grade. The final amended policy was referred to the full School Committee for formal adoption in late 2023.

threads.name: District Reporting and Calendar Planning
threads.summary: The body manages the schedule of administrative reports, including recurring updates on student achievements, English learner enrollment, and MSBA progress. The committee has moved to consolidate social-emotional learning reports and set specific deadlines for annual reports on special education legal fees. Ongoing reviews are conducted to determine which historical report requests should remain as live presentations versus written updates.
